donor_domain: statistics / decision theory; concurrency theory; information theory
donor_source_ids: Blackwell 1951 (Comparison of experiments); Blackwell 1953 (Equivalent comparisons of experiments); Larsen-Skou 1991 (bisimulation, context); Tishby-Pereira-Bialek 1999 (information bottleneck, context)
donor_structure: Blackwell order: experiment E dominates F iff F is a garbling of E (F's signal = E's signal passed through a stochastic kernel); then E is at least as valuable as F for EVERY decision problem and loss. Probabilistic bisimulation: states indistinguishable by all probabilistic observations iff related by a largest bisimulation (kernel-observational equivalence). Information bottleneck: minimal sufficient statistics as rate-distortion trade-off.
target_structure: representation sufficiency: when does one internal representation of the search state suffice for every downstream query of the process (decision, control, prediction) - i.e., a summary that loses nothing relevant.
mapping: experiment/signal -> state representation; garbling kernel -> lossy summarization map; decision problem -> downstream HSG consumer (proposal kernel, verifier, burden estimate); dominance -> 'representation rho suffices over rho' iff rho' factors as rho followed by a kernel.
preserved_relations: order independence: sufficiency order holds for every downstream loss (Blackwell's central invariance)
post-processing never helps: applying any stochastic post-map to a sufficient representation cannot increase decision value (data-processing inequality shared by all three donor families)
lumpability/bisimulation instance: quotienting by an observation-kernel equivalence preserves behaviour exactly when the kernel is a congruence for the dynamics
known_broken_relations: Blackwell order is partial (incomparable experiments exist) - sufficiency is not a total ranking of representations
computational cost of maintaining the full sufficient statistic is not part of the donor theory (HSG burden must be charged separately); 'sufficient but unaffordable' representations exist
under distribution shift (ecology drift, vi removal) a once-sufficient representation can cease to be sufficient; donor theory is fixed-prior
unknown_correspondences: relative sufficiency under bounded computation (sufficiency vs. burden trade-off surface) has no donor-owned theorem
whether HSG verifier soundness can be re-read as sufficiency of the verification channel is untested
assumptions_added: downstream consumers are decision problems measurable w.r.t. the representation sigma-algebra
fixed task distribution (ecology) during the comparison
candidate_theorem: Representation rho dominates rho' for all downstream consumers iff rho' = K o rho for some stochastic kernel K (garbling); minimal sufficient representation exists and is unique up to isomorphism under fixed ecology.
strongest_parent: Blackwell 1951/1953 (dominance iff garbling; verified standard form, already in HSG ledger as R3 OWNS)
route: L2 read of Blackwell order; cross-validated against bisimulation (kernel congruence) and IB (rate-distortion) - all three instantiate the same post-processing order
status_rationale: parent theorem standard and directly instantiates; two independent donor families (bisimulation, IB) corroborate the same order; no counterexample found within the fixed-ecology scope. Ecology-drift caveat recorded as assumption, not defect.
